reference_facts: Jewellery is the largest single source of annual gold demand.
Investment demand for bars, coins and exchange-traded funds and purchases by central banks are also major components of gold demand.
Gold is used in electronics because it conducts electricity well and does not corrode.
Gold is already used in small quantities in consumer electronics, for example as plating on connectors and as bonding wire.
Silver and copper both conduct electricity better than gold.
If the price of gold fell, gold would become more price-competitive with copper and silver as a conductor.
Because gold is priced in global markets, a decline in one demand segment does not reduce the price in proportion.
sources: World Gold Council gold demand statistics

reference_facts: Aluminium is the most abundant metal in the Earth's crust.
During the 19th century aluminium was more expensive than silver.
Aluminium was expensive before 1886 because no cheap process existed to separate it from its ore.
The Hall-Heroult electrolytic process, developed independently in 1886, made large-scale aluminium smelting possible.
The Bayer process, patented in 1888, refines bauxite into alumina for smelting.
Aluminium smelting consumes large amounts of electricity, so electricity prices strongly affect the production cost.
After the Hall-Heroult process was adopted, the price of aluminium fell from precious-metal levels to commodity levels.
Nuclear fission of uranium-235 releases heat inside the reactor core.
The heat produced by fission is used to boil water into steam.
The steam drives a turbine that is connected to an electrical generator.
The generator converts the rotation of the turbine into electricity.
Control rods absorb neutrons and are used to control the rate of the chain reaction.
Most commercial power reactors are light-water reactors, either pressurised water reactors or boiling water reactors.
Natural uranium contains about 0.7 percent uranium-235 and is usually enriched to between 3 and 5 percent for light-water reactor fuel.
Reactor number 4 at the Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant exploded on 26 April 1986.
The accident happened during a delayed safety test of the turbine running down.
Before the explosion the operators had reduced the reactor power sharply, which left the reactor unstable at low power.
Before the explosion the operators withdrew most of the control rods in order to raise the power again.
The RBMK reactor had a positive void coefficient, so forming steam increased reactivity.
The graphite tips of the RBMK control rods caused an initial increase in reactivity when the emergency shutdown was triggered.
A steam explosion destroyed the reactor and released radioactive material into the atmosphere.
The Chernobyl reactor had no full containment structure of the kind used in Western pressurised water reactors.
Lithium-ion cells store roughly 150 to 250 watt-hours per kilogram, while lead-acid cells store roughly 30 to 50 watt-hours per kilogram.
Lithium-ion batteries are lighter than lead-acid batteries that store the same amount of energy.
Lithium-ion batteries store more energy per unit of volume than lead-acid batteries.
Lead-acid batteries cost less per kilowatt-hour of capacity than lithium-ion batteries.
Lithium-ion batteries tolerate deeper discharge and deliver more charge-discharge cycles than lead-acid batteries.
Lithium-ion batteries have a higher round-trip charging efficiency than lead-acid batteries.
Lead-acid batteries are still widely used as 12 volt starter batteries in vehicles with combustion engines.
If cabin pressure is lost at about 35,000 feet, the time of useful consciousness is roughly 30 to 60 seconds.
Loss of cabin pressure causes hypoxia, which produces confusion and then loss of consciousness.
Oxygen masks drop automatically when cabin pressure falls below a set threshold.
The flight crew must descend the aircraft to about 10,000 feet, where the air contains enough oxygen to breathe without supplemental oxygen.
Rapid decompression cools the air in the cabin and can produce a visible mist or fog.
Gas trapped in the ears, sinuses and intestines expands during decompression and can cause pain.
Passengers are told to fit their own mask before helping others because useful consciousness is lost within about a minute at cruising altitude.
sources: FAA Airplane Flying Handbook, hypoxia and altitude physiology

reference_facts: Raising the policy interest rate increases borrowing costs for households and businesses.
Higher borrowing costs reduce consumer spending and business investment.
Weaker demand reduces upward pressure on prices, which lowers inflation.
Monetary policy affects inflation with a lag, usually several quarters and sometimes up to about two years.
Higher interest rates can strengthen the currency, which makes imported goods cheaper in domestic currency.
Interest rate increases also work by lowering the inflation expectations of households and firms.
Inflation caused by supply shocks responds less to interest rate increases than inflation caused by excess demand.
sources: Bank of England and Federal Reserve explanatory material on policy lags

reference_facts: The Panama Canal opened on 15 August 1914.
Before the canal opened, ships travelling between the Atlantic and the Pacific sailed around Cape Horn or through the Strait of Magellan.
The canal shortens the voyage between New York and San Francisco by about 8,000 nautical miles.
The canal uses locks to lift ships to Gatun Lake, which lies about 26 metres above sea level.
A French attempt to build the canal in the 1880s under Ferdinand de Lesseps failed because of disease and engineering difficulties.
The United States took over the project in 1904 and completed the canal.
The dimensions of the original locks defined the Panamax limit on ship size.
A set of larger locks opened in 2016 and allows larger Neopanamax ships to transit.
The first dose of a vaccine primes the immune system and generates memory B cells and T cells.
A second dose raises antibody levels higher than the first dose alone.
The interval between doses allows germinal centre reactions in which antibodies mature and gain affinity for the antigen.
A booster dose given too soon after the first produces a weaker boost than one given after several weeks.
Antibodies produced after a second dose bind the antigen more strongly than those produced after the first dose.
Protection from a two-dose schedule generally lasts longer than protection from a single dose of the same vaccine.
Some vaccines, such as the live attenuated yellow fever vaccine, give long-lasting protection after a single dose.
The Montreal Protocol was signed in 1987.
The Montreal Protocol required countries to phase out chlorofluorocarbons and other ozone-depleting substances.
Chlorofluorocarbons release chlorine in the stratosphere, and that chlorine destroys ozone in a catalytic cycle.
Atmospheric concentrations of the substances controlled by the protocol have been declining since the late 1990s.
The Antarctic ozone hole forms each southern spring, helped by polar stratospheric clouds.
Recovery of the ozone layer is slow because chlorofluorocarbons remain in the atmosphere for decades.
Scientific assessments project that the Antarctic ozone hole will recover to 1980 values around 2066.
sources: WMO/UNEP Scientific Assessment of Ozone Depletion 2022

reference_facts: Concorde entered commercial service in 1976 and was retired in 2003.
Concorde cruised at about Mach 2 at an altitude of around 60,000 feet.
Concorde burned far more fuel per passenger than subsonic wide-body airliners.
Concorde carried about 100 passengers, while a Boeing 747 carried more than 400, so fixed costs were spread across fewer seats.
The sonic boom from supersonic flight led the United States to prohibit civil supersonic flight over land.
Only 14 Concorde aircraft entered commercial service, which kept maintenance and spare parts costs high per aircraft.
The crash of Air France Flight 4590 in 2000 and the fall in air traffic after September 2001 preceded the retirement of Concorde.
sources: US FAA rule on civil supersonic flight overland

reference_facts: Arctic sea ice floats on an ocean that is surrounded by land, while Antarctic sea ice surrounds a continent and is open to the Southern Ocean.
Most Antarctic sea ice melts each summer, so it is mainly first-year ice, while the Arctic retains more multi-year ice.
Melting sea ice raises sea level very little because floating ice already displaces a volume of water equal to its own weight.
Melting land ice, such as glaciers and the Greenland and Antarctic ice sheets, does raise sea level.
Arctic sea ice extent has declined substantially since satellite measurements began in 1979.
Antarctic sea ice extent grew slightly until 2014 and has fallen sharply since 2016.
Replacing bright sea ice with darker ocean lowers the albedo of the surface, which amplifies warming.
sources: NSIDC sea ice data and FAQ
IPCC AR6 Working Group I, chapter 9
